Things to Do in Augusta, GA: The Definitive Local Guide

Augusta, Georgia, is more than just the home of the Masters. Set along the banks of the Savannah River, this city blends Southern charm, outdoor adventure, and a rich cultural scene. Whether you're visiting for a weekend, a week, or a lifetime, there's no shortage of things to do in Augusta, GA. From strolling the Riverwalk to paddling the Savannah, here's your insider guide to the best experiences — and where to stay to make the most of your trip.

1. Explore the Augusta Riverwalk

The Augusta Riverwalk is the city's crown jewel. This paved promenade stretches along the Savannah River, offering scenic views, public art, and access to some of Augusta's best restaurants and bars. Start at the 8th Street Plaza and walk east toward the Augusta Convention Center. Along the way, you'll pass the Augusta Museum of History and the Morris Museum of Art — both worth a stop.

Local tip: Visit at sunset for a spectacular view of the river and the Georgia-Carolina bridge. The Riverwalk is also a great spot for a morning jog or a leisurely bike ride.

2. Tour the Augusta National Golf Club (Home of the Masters)

No trip to Augusta is complete without acknowledging its most famous landmark. Augusta National Golf Club hosts the Masters Tournament every April, drawing golf fans from around the world. While the course is private, you can still experience the magic by visiting during tournament week or taking a drive down Washington Road. For golf enthusiasts, the Augusta Museum of History has a permanent exhibit on the Masters and the city's golf legacy.

Local tip: If you're in town during Masters Week, avoid the traffic on Washington Road by using the back routes. Staying at a riverfront property like KJ Augusta Rentals gives you a private back road to the course — just 15 minutes away.

3. Get Out on the Water: Kayaking and Boating on the Savannah River

The Savannah River is Augusta's playground. Rent a kayak or bring your own and explore the calm waters, spotting wildlife like herons, turtles, and even the occasional bald eagle. For a guided experience, check out local outfitters like Kayak Augusta. If you prefer motorized fun, rent a boat from Savannah River Boat Rentals and cruise down the river.

Local tip: Stay right on the river at KJ Augusta Rentals, where six kayaks are included with your stay. Paddle from your private dock and enjoy the water at your own pace.

4. Discover Augusta's Cultural Scene

Augusta has a thriving arts and culture scene. The Morris Museum of Art features Southern art from the 19th century to the present. The Augusta Museum of History offers exhibits on the city's history, including its role in the Civil War and the textile industry. For live entertainment, check out the Imperial Theatre, a restored 1918 vaudeville house that hosts concerts, plays, and comedy shows.

Local tip: First Thursday of every month, downtown Augusta comes alive with the Art Walk — galleries open their doors, and local artists showcase their work.

5. Enjoy Outdoor Recreation at Phinizy Swamp Nature Park

Just minutes from downtown, Phinizy Swamp Nature Park is a 1,100-acre wildlife sanctuary with trails, boardwalks, and observation decks. It's a birder's paradise, with over 200 species recorded. Bring your camera and a pair of binoculars — you might spot an alligator or a river otter.

Local tip: The park is free to enter and open daily from dawn to dusk. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water, as some trails are unpaved.

6. Tee Off at a Local Golf Course

Augusta is a golfer's paradise. Beyond Augusta National, there are several public courses worth playing. The Bartram Trail Golf Club offers a challenging 18-hole layout, while Augusta Municipal Golf Course is a budget-friendly option with great views. For a unique experience, try the Pine Grove Golf Club, known for its friendly staff and well-maintained greens.

Local tip: Many courses offer twilight rates — play in the late afternoon for discounted green fees.

7. Savor Southern Cuisine

Augusta's food scene is a delicious blend of Southern classics and modern innovation. Start your day with shrimp and grits at The French Market Grille, then grab lunch at Southern Smoke for authentic barbecue. For dinner, Calvert's offers upscale Southern fare in a historic setting. And don't miss The Bee's Knees for craft cocktails and small plates.

Local tip: Many downtown restaurants offer happy hour specials from 4–7 PM on weekdays.

8. Catch a Minor League Baseball Game

Cheer on the Augusta GreenJackets, the Single-A affiliate of the Atlanta Braves, at SRP Park in North Augusta. The stadium is family-friendly, with promotions, fireworks, and a great view of the river. Even if you're not a baseball fan, the atmosphere is worth experiencing.

Local tip: Tickets are affordable, and the park offers a variety of food options, including local favorites.
